title: Austria-Hungary
capsule: This entry tracks the Hungarian national movement and its institutional expression from the failed 1848–49 revolution through the era of the Austro-Hungarian dual monarchy. After the revolution led by Lajos Kossuth was crushed by Habsburg and Russian forces in 1849, Hungarian nationalists pursued autonomy by constitutional means, achieving the Ausgleich (Compromise) of 1867 negotiated chiefly by Ferenc Deák, which granted the Kingdom of Hungary internal self-government within the dual monarchy. Hungarian liberal-national parties dominated Budapest politics down to the early twentieth century, pressing Magyarization and demands for greater independence from Vienna. The defeat of Austria-Hungary in World War I dissolved the monarchy in 1918, and the Treaty of Trianon (1920) stripped the new Hungarian state of roughly two-thirds of its pre-war territory.
